# Calcnate: calculator reference

> The formulas, rules, sources and FAQs from every English calculator page on calcnate.com, extracted from the live pages. Estimates for guidance only, not legal or financial advice. Index: https://calcnate.com/llms.txt

## United Arab Emirates

### UAE Final Settlement Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/final-settlement-calculator/
Your complete full & final figure — gratuity plus leave encashment, notice pay and pending salary, minus deductions. Per UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Gratuity | 21 days/yr (first 5), 30 days/yr after — on basic
Leave encashment | Unused annual-leave days × basic daily wage
Notice pay | Notice days × gross daily wage (if terminated without notice)
Pending salary | Unpaid worked days × gross daily wage
Leave is encashed at basic wage. Everything must be paid within 14 days of contract end. Source: UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 .
#### Questions
Q: What is included in a UAE full and final settlement?
A: Gratuity, encashment of unused annual leave (at basic wage), pending unpaid salary, notice-period pay if the employer ended the contract without notice, minus documented deductions like loans or advances.
Q: Is annual leave encashed on basic or gross salary?
A: Unused annual leave is encashed at the basic wage.
Q: When must the final settlement be paid?
A: Within 14 days of the contract end date.
Q: Do I lose gratuity if I resign?
A: No — since Decree-Law 33/2021, resignation no longer reduces gratuity for anyone with over 1 year of service.

### Gratuity Calculator UAE
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/gratuity-calculator/
End-of-service gratuity per MOHRE rules — UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021. Same result whether you resign or are terminated after 1 year.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
First 5 years | 21 days of basic salary per year
Beyond 5 years | 30 days of basic salary per year
Under 1 year | No gratuity
Maximum | 2 years' total wages
Daily wage = basic monthly salary ÷ 30. Gratuity is on BASIC salary only (allowances excluded). Source: UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 .
#### Questions
Q: Do I get full gratuity if I resign in the UAE?
A: Yes. Under Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 (in force since Feb 2022), resignation no longer reduces gratuity. Anyone with more than one year of continuous service receives the full calculation whether they resign or are terminated.
Q: Is UAE gratuity on basic or gross salary?
A: Basic salary only. Housing, transport and other allowances are excluded.
Q: Does this apply in free zones like JAFZA or DMCC?
A: Yes — most free zones follow the federal labour law. DIFC and ADGM are exceptions with their own regimes (DIFC uses the DEWS savings scheme).
Q: What is the maximum UAE gratuity?
A: Total gratuity cannot exceed two years' worth of wages.
Q: When must my gratuity be paid?
A: All end-of-service dues must be paid within 14 days of the contract end date.

### UAE Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused UAE annual leave — encashment is on your BASIC salary (not gross), per Federal Decree-Law 33/2021, Article 29 and Cabinet Resolution 1/2022.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 30 calendar days/year after 1 year of service; 2 days/month for 6 months-1 year
Encashment on end of service | (Basic monthly salary ÷ 30) × unused days — BASIC salary only
Leave taken during employment | Paid at full wage (basic + allowances) — different from encashment
Carry-over | Up to half of unused leave may carry to the next year, or be cashed by agreement
Encashment on termination uses BASIC salary even though leave taken during employment is paid at full wage — a common point of confusion. Cross-checked against U.AE government portal . Source: Khaleej Times (legal) .
#### Questions
Q: Is UAE leave encashment on basic or gross salary?
A: Basic salary only — even though leave taken while still employed is paid at your full wage (basic plus allowances).
Q: How many annual leave days do I earn in the UAE?
A: 30 calendar days per year once you pass 1 year of service; 2 calendar days per month if you have 6 months to 1 year of service.
Q: Can I carry my leave over to next year?
A: Up to half of your unused leave can carry over, or you can agree with your employer to be paid cash for the carried-forward portion.
Q: When is leave encashed?
A: Typically at the end of your employment for any unused balance — see our UAE Final Settlement Calculator for the full end-of-service picture.

### UAE Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in the UAE and what it's worth — per Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, Article 30.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Total maternity leave | 60 calendar days
First 45 days | Full pay (100%)
Remaining 15 days | Half pay (50%)
Minimum service required | None — applies from day one of employment
If newborn is sick/disabled | +30 days full pay, +30 further days unpaid (with medical certificate)
Nursing breaks after return | Up to 1 hour/day, fully paid, for 6 months
Who pays | Employer, in full
Also available: 45 days unpaid leave for pregnancy/childbirth-related illness, on a medical certificate. Source: UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 (Art. 30) .
#### Questions
Q: How many days of paid maternity leave do I get in the UAE?
A: 60 calendar days total: the first 45 days at full (100%) pay, and the remaining 15 days at half (50%) pay — under Article 30 of Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021.
Q: Do I need a minimum length of service to qualify for UAE maternity leave?
A: No — it applies from your very first day of employment. There's no tenure requirement, unlike some other UAE benefits.
Q: What if my baby is born sick or with a disability?
A: You're entitled to a further 30 days of fully paid leave, plus an additional 30 days unpaid, to care for a sick or disabled newborn, with a medical certificate.
Q: Do I get paid breaks for nursing after I return to work?
A: Yes — up to 1 hour per day, fully paid, for 6 months after you return from maternity leave.
Q: Who pays for UAE maternity leave — the employer or the government?
A: Your employer pays it in full. There's no separate government or social-insurance maternity fund for the private sector in the UAE.

### UAE Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/notice-period-calculator/
How much notice you owe — or are owed — under UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021, including the probation-period sub-rules.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Standard notice (post-probation) | 30-90 days, as agreed in your contract — same for employer and employee (Art. 43)
Probation — employer ends it | At least 14 days notice
Probation — you resign to join another UAE employer | At least 30 days (1 month) notice
Probation — you resign and leave the UAE / no new local job | At least 14 days notice
If notice is not served | Either side may pay the other's salary for the unserved notice days instead
Notice must be in writing. During notice the contract stays fully in force — full pay and duties continue. Cross-checked against MOHRE (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021) . Source: Chambers and Partners .
#### Questions
Q: What is the minimum notice period in the UAE?
A: 30 days for a standard (post-probation) contract, and it cannot exceed 90 days — the exact figure is whatever your contract states within that range, per Article 43 of Federal Decree-Law 33/2021.
Q: Is the UAE notice period the same for employer and employee?
A: Yes — Article 43 requires the same notice period from both sides for a standard contract.
Q: What is the UAE probation notice period?
A: If your employer ends it, at least 14 days. If you resign to join another UAE employer, at least 30 days. If you resign and are leaving the UAE or not taking new local work, at least 14 days (Article 44).
Q: Can my employer make me leave immediately and pay me instead of serving notice?
A: Yes — either party can waive the notice period by paying the other side's salary for the remaining notice days.
Q: Do I still get paid during my notice period?
A: Yes, in full, and your employer must give you one unpaid day off per week (with 3 days notice) to search for a new job.

### UAE Probation Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/probation-period-calculator/
How much notice is legally required to end employment during probation in the UAE — the rule differs depending on who's ending it and why. Per Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, Article 9.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Maximum probation length | 6 months from your actual start date (no extension; cannot be repeated with the same employer)
Employer ends employment during probation | ≥14 days' notice
You resign to join another UAE employer | ≥30 days' (1 month) notice
You resign to leave your job / the country | ≥14 days' notice
Breach of notice | The breaching party owes wages for the notice shortfall
Gratuity during probation | None — gratuity requires 1+ year of service (Art. 51); probation time counts toward that year if employment continues
Notice pay in lieu is estimated on your monthly salary ÷ 30. Your contract may specify a longer notice period than the statutory minimum. Source: UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 (Art. 9) .
#### Questions
Q: How long can probation last in the UAE?
A: Up to 6 months from your actual start date. It cannot be extended, and you cannot be placed on probation twice by the same employer.
Q: How much notice do I need to give if I resign during UAE probation?
A: It depends: 30 days' notice if you're joining another employer inside the UAE, or 14 days' notice if you're leaving your job entirely (not joining another UAE employer) — under Article 9 of Federal Decree-Law No. 33/2021.
Q: How much notice does my employer need to give to end my probation?
A: At least 14 days' written notice, the same as if you were resigning to leave the country.
Q: Do I get gratuity if I'm let go during UAE probation?
A: No — end-of-service gratuity under UAE law only starts accruing after you complete 1 full year of continuous service (Article 51). A probation period (max 6 months) never reaches that threshold on its own.
Q: What happens if my employer doesn't give me proper notice?
A: Whichever party fails to give the required notice owes the other side wages for the shortfall in the notice period.

### UAE Unemployment Insurance (ILOE) Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uae/unemployment-insurance-calculator/
Check your eligibility and estimate your Involuntary Loss of Employment (ILOE) insurance payout — separate from end-of-service gratuity. Per Federal Decree-Law No. 13 of 2022.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Category A — basic salary ≤ AED 16,000 | Premium AED 5/month · payout capped at AED 10,000/month
Category B — basic salary > AED 16,000 | Premium AED 10/month · payout capped at AED 20,000/month
Monthly compensation | 60% of your average basic salary over the last 6 months (subject to the category cap above)
Maximum duration | Up to 3 months per claim, or until you find new work — whichever comes first
Lifetime aggregate cap | Total ILOE payouts across your entire UAE working life cannot exceed 12 monthly benefits, no matter how many separate claims
Minimum subscription | At least 12 consecutive months of paid premiums before you can claim
Claim window | Must be submitted within 30 days of the employment relationship ending
First payment | Typically disbursed within about 14 days of an approved claim
Only involuntary job loss qualifies — resignation and termination for disciplinary reasons/gross misconduct are excluded. Investors/business owners, domestic workers, workers under 18, and retirees drawing a pension who take new work cannot subscribe. Rates last verified July 2026 — always confirm at iloe.ae, as scheme parameters can be revised administratively. Source: Official ILOE portal (iloe.ae) & U.AE government portal .
#### Questions
Q: Who is eligible to claim UAE unemployment insurance (ILOE)?
A: You must have subscribed and paid ILOE premiums for at least 12 consecutive months, lost your job involuntarily (not by resignation or disciplinary termination), and not be in an excluded category (business owner/investor, domestic worker, under 18, or a pensioned retiree in new employment). You must also file your claim within 30 days of your employment ending.
Q: How much does ILOE pay per month?
A: 60% of your average basic salary over your last 6 months of work — capped at AED 10,000/month if you're a Category A subscriber (basic salary AED 16,000 or below) or AED 20,000/month if you're Category B (basic salary above AED 16,000).
Q: What is Category A vs Category B in ILOE?
A: Category A covers a basic salary of AED 16,000 or below (premium AED 5/month, payout capped at AED 10,000/month). Category B covers a basic salary above AED 16,000 (premium AED 10/month, payout capped at AED 20,000/month). You're placed in whichever category matches your basic salary.
Q: How long does ILOE pay out for?
A: Up to 3 consecutive months per claim, or until you start new employment — whichever happens first. Across your entire working life in the UAE, total ILOE payments (from any number of claims) cannot exceed 12 monthly benefits in aggregate.
Q: Can I claim ILOE if I resign?
A: No. ILOE only covers involuntary loss of employment — redundancy, company closure, non-renewal of contract by the employer and similar. Voluntary resignation and termination for disciplinary reasons or gross misconduct are not covered.
Q: Is ILOE the same as my end-of-service gratuity?
A: No — they're completely separate. Gratuity is an end-of-service benefit paid by your employer based on your years of service (see our UAE Gratuity Calculator ). ILOE is a government-mandated unemployment insurance payout, funded by your own small monthly premium, that only applies if you lose your job involuntarily. You can be entitled to both at the same time.

## Saudi Arabia

### Saudi End of Service Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/saudi/end-of-service-calculator/
End-of-service award (ESB) per Saudi Labour Law — half a month's wage per year for the first 5 years, a full month after, with resignation reductions.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
First 5 years | ½ month wage per year
Beyond 5 years | 1 month wage per year
Resign 2–5 yrs | ⅓ of the award
Resign 5–10 yrs | ⅔ of the award
Resign 10+ yrs / any termination | Full award
Calculated on the last wage (basic + regular allowances). Pick 'Resigned' to apply the reduction tiers. Source: Saudi HRSD .
#### Questions
Q: How is end of service calculated in Saudi Arabia?
A: Half a month's wage for each of the first five years and a full month's wage for each year beyond five, based on your last wage. Resignation reduces the award unless you have 10+ years.
Q: Do I get end of service if I resign in Saudi Arabia?
A: Yes, but reduced: nothing under 2 years, one-third for 2–5 years, two-thirds for 5–10 years, and the full amount at 10+ years. Employer termination always pays the full award.
Q: Is Saudi ESB on basic or total salary?
A: On the last wage including regular allowances, which is broader than the UAE's basic-only rule.
Q: Is there a cap on Saudi end of service?
A: No statutory ceiling on the total award.

### Saudi Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/saudi/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused Saudi annual leave — encashment is mandatory on end of service, on your last actual wage, per Labour Law Articles 109 and 111.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 21 days/year for under 5 years of service; 30 days/year at 5+ years
Encashment during employment | Not allowed — leave cannot be waived or exchanged for cash while still working (Art. 109)
Encashment on end of service | Mandatory — (last wage ÷ 30) × unused days (Art. 111)
Wage basis | Actual wage — basic wage plus regular allowances (Art. 2)
Article 109 specifically bans cashing out leave while still employed — encashment only becomes payable once employment ends, under the separate Article 111. Cross-checked against payrollmiddleeast.com . Source: HRSD .
#### Questions
Q: How much annual leave do Saudi employees earn?
A: 21 days per year with under 5 years of service, rising to 30 days per year once you complete 5 consecutive years with the same employer.
Q: Can I cash out my leave while still working in Saudi Arabia?
A: No — Article 109 prohibits waiving or exchanging leave for money during employment. It can only be encashed when your employment ends (Article 111).
Q: What salary is used for Saudi leave encashment?
A: Your actual wage — basic wage plus regular cash allowances — the same broad definition used for end-of-service benefits.
Q: Can I postpone my leave instead?
A: Yes, by mutual agreement with your employer, for up to 3 years.

### Saudi Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/saudi/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in Saudi Arabia under the current (2025-amended) Labor Law — 12 weeks at full pay, no minimum service required.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Total paid maternity leave | 12 weeks (84 days) at full (100%) pay
Mandatory post-delivery portion | At least 6 weeks
Can start before delivery | Up to 4 weeks before the expected date, on medical certificate
Minimum service required | None — the pre-2025 tenure tiers were removed
If newborn is sick / needs continuous care | +1 further month fully paid, plus another month unpaid
Unpaid extension (any case) | 1 further month available
Who pays | Employer, in full
This reflects the CURRENT law (effective ~Feb 2025), which increased leave from the previous 10 weeks and removed the old tenure-based pay tiers (full pay ≥3yrs / half pay 1–3yrs / unpaid Saudi Labor Law, Article 151, as amended by Royal Decree M/44 of 1446H (effective ~Feb 2025) .
#### Questions
Q: How many weeks of maternity leave do I get in Saudi Arabia?
A: 12 weeks (84 days), all at full (100%) pay — increased from 10 weeks under an amendment to Article 151 effective around February 2025.
Q: Do I need a minimum length of service to get full pay in Saudi Arabia?
A: No, not anymore. The 2025 amendment removed the previous tenure-based tiers (which used to give full pay only at 3+ years of service, half pay for 1–3 years, and unpaid under 1 year). Now it's 12 weeks full pay regardless of tenure.
Q: How much of Saudi maternity leave must be taken after delivery?
A: At least 6 weeks must be taken immediately after the birth. The rest of your 12 weeks can be started up to 4 weeks before your expected delivery date, on a medical certificate.
Q: What if my baby needs special care in Saudi Arabia?
A: You can get a further month fully paid, plus an additional month unpaid, if your newborn is sick or has special needs requiring your continuous care.
Q: Is Saudi maternity leave paid by the employer or GOSI?
A: Your employer pays your salary during the leave. Saudi's General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) has separately introduced a maternity-related benefit under its newer social-insurance regime for registered contributors — but the employer-paid salary under the Labor Law is the core entitlement covered here.

### Saudi Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/saudi/notice-period-calculator/
Notice period for ending an indefinite Saudi employment contract under the amended Labour Law Article 75, in force since 18 February 2025.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
You resign | 30 days notice (any pay frequency)
Employer ends it — monthly-paid worker | 60 days notice
Employer ends it — other pay frequency | 30 days notice
If notice is not served | The party at fault pays the other's wage for the notice period
Applies to indefinite-term contracts. Wage basis follows Saudi Labour Law Article 2 (basic wage plus regular cash allowances) and is calculated on a 30-day month. Cross-checked against King & Spalding . Source: Dentons .
#### Questions
Q: How long is the notice period in Saudi Arabia?
A: Since the amendment effective 18 February 2025: 30 days if you resign, or if your employer ends a non-monthly-paid contract; 60 days if your employer ends a monthly-paid contract.
Q: Did the Saudi notice period change recently?
A: Yes. Before the amendment, both sides owed 60 days (monthly-paid) or 30 days (other). The employee side was reduced to a flat 30 days regardless of pay frequency.
Q: What happens if the notice period is not honoured?
A: The party who fails to give proper notice must compensate the other with wages equal to the notice period.
Q: What if my resignation gets no employer response?
A: If your employer does not respond within 30 days, your resignation is automatically accepted — though they may postpone acceptance up to 60 days with written justification.

### Saudi Probation Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/saudi/probation-period-calculator/
How probation works in Saudi Arabia under the current (2025-amended) Labor Law — and why the notice period is set by your contract, not a fixed number in the law.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Maximum probation length | Up to 180 days, set directly in the contract (since the Feb 2025 amendment — previously 90 days by default, extendable to 180 only via a separate agreement)
Termination rights | Mutual by default since the 2025 amendment (previously could be reserved to one party only)
Statutory notice period | None fixed by law — governed by your employment contract
Gratuity/compensation on probation termination | None owed by either party
Repeating probation | Not allowed with the same employer for the same role (exceptions: a different role, or 6+ months since prior employment ended)
This reflects the CURRENT law after the February 2025 amendment. Before that, probation defaulted to 90 days (extendable to 180 by separate written agreement) and termination rights could be one-sided if the contract said so. Source: Saudi Labor Law, Article 53, as amended by Royal Decree M/44 of 1446H (effective ~Feb 2025) .
#### Questions
Q: How long can probation last in Saudi Arabia?
A: Up to 180 days, which can now be set directly in the employment contract from the start (since the amendment effective around February 2025, under Royal Decree M/44). Before that amendment, the default was 90 days, extendable to 180 only through a separate written agreement.
Q: How much notice do I need to give during probation in Saudi Arabia?
A: Saudi Labor Law itself does not fix a mandatory notice period for ending employment during probation — this is left to your employment contract. Check what your contract says; if it's silent, no statutory minimum applies.
Q: Can only my employer end my probation in Saudi Arabia, or can I as well?
A: Since the 2025 amendment, termination rights during probation are mutual by default for both employer and employee — previously, a contract could reserve this right to just one side.
Q: Do I get gratuity if let go during Saudi probation?
A: No — no end-of-service gratuity or other compensation is owed by either party for a termination that happens during the probation period.
Q: Can I be put on probation twice by the same employer in Saudi Arabia?
A: Not for the same role — unless you're taking on a different position, or at least 6 months have passed since your previous employment with that employer ended.

## Qatar

### Qatar Gratuity Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/qatar/end-of-service-calculator/
End-of-service gratuity per Qatar Labour Law — at least 3 weeks (21 days) of basic wage for every completed year of service.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Per year of service | At least 3 weeks (21 days) basic wage
Minimum service | 1 year
Basis | Last basic wage
Resignation | Same entitlement once 1+ year
21 days is the statutory minimum; your contract may give more. Excludes allowances. Source: Qatar Labour Law (Art. 54) .
#### Questions
Q: How is gratuity calculated in Qatar?
A: At least three weeks (21 days) of your last basic wage for each completed year of service, once you have worked at least one year. Your contract can provide more but not less.
Q: Does resignation affect Qatar gratuity?
A: No. Once you complete one year, you receive the gratuity whether you resign or are terminated.
Q: Is Qatar gratuity on basic or total pay?
A: On the basic wage — allowances are excluded.
Q: What is the minimum service for Qatar gratuity?
A: One completed year of continuous service.

### Qatar Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/qatar/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused Qatar annual leave on your basic wage, per Labour Law Article 79.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 3 weeks (21 days)/year for under 5 years of service; 4 weeks (28 days)/year at 5+ years
Wage basis | Basic wage, as applicable on the date the leave falls due
Carry-over | Up to half of unused leave may be carried to the next year by request
Encashment | Compensation in lieu of leave accrued but not taken
Applies once an employee has completed 1 full year of continuous service; leave before that accrues on a pro-rata basis. Cross-checked against Ministry of Labour, Qatar (official Facebook post citing Article 79) . Source: Al Meezan — Qatar Legal Portal .
#### Questions
Q: How much annual leave do Qatar employees earn?
A: 3 weeks (21 days) per year with under 5 years of service, rising to 4 weeks (28 days) per year once you complete 5 years, under Article 79 of the Labour Law.
Q: What salary is leave encashment based on?
A: Your basic wage, as it stood on the date the leave became due.
Q: Can unused leave carry over in Qatar?
A: Yes — up to half of it can be carried forward to the next year on request.
Q: When is leave encashed?
A: When it is accrued but not taken — most commonly settled as part of your final dues when employment ends.

### Qatar Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/qatar/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave private-sector employees are entitled to in Qatar, and what it's worth — per Labour Law No. 14 of 2004, Article 96.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Total paid maternity leave | 50 days at full (100%) pay
Minimum post-delivery portion | At least 35 days must fall after delivery
Eligibility | More than 1 year of continuous service with the employer
Further unpaid leave if unwell | Up to 60 days, with medical certificate
Job protection | Termination during maternity leave is prohibited (Art. 98)
Who pays | Employer, in full
Sector | Private sector, under Labour Law 14/2004 — a separate 2025 law gives public-sector staff 3 months
This covers PRIVATE-sector employees. Public-sector employees are covered by a separate, more generous law (Law No. 25 of 2025 amending the Civil Human Resources Law) not calculated here. Source: Qatar Labour Law No. 14/2004 (Art. 96, Art. 98) .
#### Questions
Q: How many days of paid maternity leave do I get in Qatar?
A: 50 days at full pay, under Article 96 of Labour Law No. 14/2004, for private-sector employees with more than 1 year of continuous service.
Q: What's the eligibility requirement for Qatar maternity leave?
A: You need more than 1 year of continuous service with your employer. Without that, this specific paid entitlement under Article 96 does not apply.
Q: How much of Qatar's maternity leave must be after delivery?
A: At least 35 of the 50 days must fall after the birth.
Q: Does this apply to public-sector employees in Qatar too?
A: No — public-sector employees are covered by a separate, more generous law (a 2025 amendment to the Civil Human Resources Law giving 3 months, up to 6 for twins/disability). This calculator covers private-sector employees under Labour Law 14/2004.
Q: Can I be fired while on maternity leave in Qatar?
A: No — Article 98 of the Labour Law separately prohibits termination during maternity leave.

### Qatar Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/qatar/notice-period-calculator/
Notice period for ending an employment contract in Qatar under Labour Law Article 49, for workers paid monthly or annually.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
5 years of service or less | 1 month notice
More than 5 years of service | 2 months notice
If notice is not honoured | Compensation equal to the wage for the unserved notice period
Applies to workers paid monthly or annually — the standard case for most employees. Other pay arrangements (daily/weekly/hourly) follow a shorter scale under the same article. Cross-checked against Al Tamimi & Company . Source: Mondaq .
#### Questions
Q: How much notice is required in Qatar?
A: For workers paid monthly or annually: 1 month if you have 5 years of service or less, 2 months if you have more than 5 years, per Article 49 of the Labour Law.
Q: Is the notice period the same for the employer and employee?
A: Yes — Article 49 sets the same period for whichever side is ending the contract, with no reason required.
Q: What if the notice period is not observed?
A: The party ending the contract without proper notice must pay the other the full wage for the notice period (or its remaining part).
Q: Does this apply to fixed-term contracts too?
A: Since a 2020 amendment, Article 49's notice-with-no-reason option applies to both indefinite and fixed-term contracts, not just indefinite ones.

## Kuwait

### Kuwait Indemnity Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/kuwait/indemnity-calculator/
End-of-service indemnity per Kuwait Labour Law — 15 days' pay per year for the first 5 years, a full month after, capped at 18 months' pay.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
First 5 years | 15 days pay per year
Beyond 5 years | 1 month pay per year
Daily wage | Monthly ÷ 26
Resign 3–5 yrs | ½ of indemnity
Resign 5–10 yrs | ⅔ of indemnity
Cap | 18 months' total pay
Based on full remuneration (basic + regular allowances), daily wage = monthly ÷ 26. Total capped at 1.5 years' pay. Source: Kuwait Labour Law summary .
#### Questions
Q: How is indemnity calculated in Kuwait?
A: Fifteen days' pay for each of the first five years and a full month's pay for each year after five, using a daily wage of monthly pay ÷ 26, capped at 18 months' total pay.
Q: Do I get indemnity if I resign in Kuwait?
A: Yes, reduced: nothing under 3 years, half for 3–5 years, two-thirds for 5–10 years, and the full amount at 10+ years.
Q: What is the maximum Kuwait indemnity?
A: Total indemnity is capped at 18 months (1.5 years) of pay.
Q: Is Kuwait indemnity on basic or full pay?
A: On full remuneration including regular allowances.

### Kuwait Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/kuwait/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused Kuwait annual leave — the daily wage divisor is 26, not 30, matching Kuwait's indemnity calculation.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 30 days/year after 1 year of service
Daily wage divisor | Monthly wage ÷ 26 (not 30)
Encashment | (Monthly wage ÷ 26) × unused leave days
On end of service | Unused balance is settled as part of final dues
The ÷26 divisor matches the one used for Kuwait indemnity — both reflect a 6-day work week convention rather than a flat 30-day month. Cross-checked against masdareor.com . Source: HLB HAMT — Guide on Statutory Leaves in Kuwait .
#### Questions
Q: How much annual leave do Kuwait employees earn?
A: 30 days per year once you complete 1 year of service, under Kuwait's Labour Law No. 6 of 2010.
Q: Why is Kuwait's leave divisor 26, not 30?
A: Kuwait's daily-wage convention for leave (and indemnity) divides the monthly wage by 26 to reflect a 6-day working week, rather than a flat calendar-day divisor.
Q: Can I get paid for unused leave while still working?
A: Employers may agree to encash unused leave during employment; it is also settled as part of your final dues if you leave the company.
Q: Is Kuwait leave pay on basic or full wage?
A: Full monthly remuneration is generally used, consistent with how the same wage figure is used for Kuwait's end-of-service indemnity.

### Kuwait Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/kuwait/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in Kuwait and what it's worth — per Labour Law No. 6 of 2010, Article 24.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Total paid maternity leave | 70 days at full (100%) pay
Timing | Within the period surrounding childbirth
Further unpaid childcare leave | Up to 4 months, on request — counts toward service/gratuity
Nursing breaks after return | 2 hours/day, paid, for up to 2 years
Job protection | Termination during maternity leave or due to pregnancy is unlawful
Who pays | Employer, in full
Daily wage estimated as monthly wage ÷ 26, consistent with Kuwait's standard end-of-service wage-basis convention. We could not independently verify a specific before/after-delivery day split, so we show the total only. Source: Kuwait Labour Law No. 6/2010 (Art. 24) .
#### Questions
Q: How many days of paid maternity leave do I get in Kuwait?
A: 70 days at full pay, under Article 24 of Labour Law No. 6 of 2010, taken around the time of childbirth.
Q: Does taking maternity leave in Kuwait reduce my annual leave?
A: No — the 70-day maternity leave is separate from and doesn't reduce your other leave entitlements, such as annual leave.
Q: Can I take more time off after my 70 days of maternity leave in Kuwait?
A: Yes — at your request, your employer may grant a further unpaid leave of up to 4 months for childcare. That unpaid time still counts toward your length of service and eventual gratuity.
Q: Do I get paid nursing breaks after returning to work in Kuwait?
A: Yes — a 2-hour paid nursing break each day, for up to 2 years after you return from maternity leave.

### Kuwait Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/kuwait/notice-period-calculator/
Notice period for ending an indefinite Kuwait employment contract — 3 months for monthly-paid workers, 1 month for others.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Monthly-paid worker | 3 months notice
Other pay frequency | 1 month notice
If notice is not honoured | Compensation equal to the wage for the notice period
Applies to indefinite-term (unlimited) contracts. Either party may waive the notice period by paying the equivalent wage instead. Cross-checked against Wefaq Law . Source: Al Razzaq Law Firm .
#### Questions
Q: How much notice must be given in Kuwait?
A: For an indefinite contract: 3 months if you are paid monthly, 1 month if you are paid another way (daily, weekly, hourly), under Kuwait's Labour Law No. 6 of 2010.
Q: Is the notice period the same for employer and employee?
A: Yes, the same period applies to whichever side ends the contract.
Q: Can the notice period be paid instead of worked?
A: Yes — either party may waive it by paying the other's wage for the notice period.
Q: Does this apply to fixed-term contracts?
A: This rule covers indefinite (unlimited) contracts. Fixed-term contracts generally run to their end date; ending one early without cause can require compensation up to the remaining contract value.

### Kuwait Probation Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/kuwait/probation-period-calculator/
What happens if employment ends during probation in Kuwait — per Labour Law No. 6 of 2010, Article 32.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Maximum probation length | 100 working days
Notice required to end employment | None — either party may end it without notice
Compensation/indemnity owed | None — only wages already earned for days actually worked
Repeating probation | Not allowed with the same employer
Daily wage estimated as monthly wage ÷ 26, consistent with Kuwait's standard end-of-service wage-basis convention. Source: Kuwait Labour Law No. 6/2010 (Art. 32) .
#### Questions
Q: How long can probation last in Kuwait?
A: A maximum of 100 working days, under Article 32 of Labour Law No. 6 of 2010. You cannot be placed on probation more than once with the same employer.
Q: Is notice required to end employment during Kuwait probation?
A: No — either the employer or the employee can end the employment during probation without any notice period.
Q: What compensation is owed if I'm let go during Kuwait probation?
A: None beyond your wages already earned for days you actually worked — no indemnity, severance, or end-of-service benefit is owed for a probation-period termination.
Q: Can I quit without notice during probation in Kuwait?
A: Yes — the right to end employment without notice during probation applies to both the employer and the employee.

## Bahrain

### Bahrain Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/bahrain/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused Bahrain annual leave on your gross wage (basic plus fixed allowances), per Labour Law Article 58.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 30 days/year, accruing at 2.5 days per month
Wage basis | Gross salary — basic plus fixed allowances (e.g. housing, transport)
Encashment formula | (Gross monthly salary ÷ 30) × unused leave days
On end of service | Unused balance is paid as part of your final settlement
Leave pay uses gross salary, unlike Bahrain's notice payment-in-lieu, which is based on basic wage plus the social allowance only — do not conflate the two wage bases. Cross-checked against Bahrain Labour Law (LMRA) . Source: HLB HAMT — Guide on Statutory Leaves in Bahrain .
#### Questions
Q: How much annual leave do Bahrain employees earn?
A: 30 days per year, accruing at 2.5 days per month of service, under Article 58 of the Labour Law.
Q: What salary is used for Bahrain leave encashment?
A: Gross salary — basic pay plus fixed allowances such as housing and transport.
Q: When is leave encashed in Bahrain?
A: When employment ends, any unused annual leave balance must be paid out in cash as part of your final settlement.
Q: Is this the same wage basis as Bahrain's notice-period payment?
A: No — notice payment in lieu uses basic wage plus the social allowance only, a narrower base than the gross salary used for leave.

### Bahrain Leaving Indemnity Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/bahrain/leaving-indemnity-calculator/
Leaving indemnity per Bahrain Labour Law — half a month's wage per year for the first 3 years, a full month after, pro-rated from day one.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
First 3 years | ½ month wage per year
Beyond 3 years | 1 month wage per year
Minimum service | None — pro-rated from day one
Basis | Last wage
For expatriate workers not enrolled in the social-insurance scheme. Pro-rated for partial years. Source: Bahrain Labour Law (Art. 116) .
#### Questions
Q: How is leaving indemnity calculated in Bahrain?
A: Half a month's wage for each of the first three years and a full month's wage for each year after three, pro-rated for partial years, based on your last wage.
Q: Is there a minimum service for Bahrain indemnity?
A: No — it accrues from day one and is pro-rated for partial years.
Q: Does resignation reduce Bahrain indemnity?
A: No standard reduction — the accrued indemnity is due on leaving.
Q: Who does this apply to?
A: Mainly expatriate workers not covered by Bahrain's social-insurance (SIO) pension scheme.

### Bahrain Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/bahrain/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in Bahrain and what it's worth — per Labour Law No. 36/2012, Article 32.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Paid maternity leave | 60 days at full (100%) wage
Optional extension | 15 further days, unpaid
Post-delivery work ban | 40 days — you must not work during this period
Number of occurrences | No cap — available every pregnancy
Minimum prior service | None stated in Article 32
Who pays | Employer, in full
A medical certificate is required. Dismissal during maternity leave is separately prohibited (Article 33). Source: Bahrain LMRA — Labour Law No. 36/2012 (Art. 32) .
#### Questions
Q: How many days of paid maternity leave do I get in Bahrain?
A: 60 days at full pay, under Article 32 of Labour Law No. 36/2012, plus an optional further 15 days unpaid if you want it.
Q: Is Bahrain maternity leave paid at full salary?
A: Yes — the 60-day statutory leave is at 100% of your wage, paid by your employer.
Q: Is there a limit on how many times I can take maternity leave in Bahrain?
A: No — the 60-day paid maternity leave applies to every pregnancy with no cap. (A separate, different entitlement — unpaid childcare leave for a child under 6 — is capped at 3 occasions; don't confuse the two.)
Q: Do I have to work right after giving birth in Bahrain?
A: No — the law requires you not to work during the 40 days immediately following delivery.

### Bahrain Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/bahrain/notice-period-calculator/
Bahrain sets one flat 30-day notice period for either party under Labour Law Article 99(a) — no sliding scale by years of service.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Either party, any length of service | 30 days notice (flat — no sliding scale)
Wage basis for payment in lieu | Basic wage + social/cost-of-living allowance (Article 47)
Longer contractual notice | Binds the employer only, not the employee
There is no tenure-based sliding scale for Bahrain notice periods — that is a common confusion with the separate leaving-indemnity formula, which does vary by years of service. Cross-checked against Bahrain Business Laws . Source: LMRA (Bahrain Labour Law, Legislation.bh) .
#### Questions
Q: How much notice is required in Bahrain?
A: A flat 30 days for either party, regardless of length of service, under Article 99(a) of the Labour Law.
Q: Does the Bahrain notice period increase with years of service?
A: No. Unlike Bahrain's leaving indemnity (which does scale with service), the notice period is a flat 30 days for everyone.
Q: Can my contract set a longer notice period?
A: Yes, but a longer period only binds the employer — you can still resign with just 30 days notice.
Q: What salary is used to calculate payment in lieu of notice?
A: Your basic wage plus any social/cost-of-living allowance, under Article 47.

### Bahrain Probation Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/bahrain/probation-period-calculator/
How much notice is legally required to end employment during probation in Bahrain, and what (if anything) is owed — per Labour Law No. 36/2012, Article 21.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Maximum probation length | 3 months (up to 6 months by Ministerial decision, specified occupations only)
Times allowed per employer | Once only
Notice to end employment during probation | At least 1 day, either party, no cause needed
Gratuity during probation | Not explicitly excluded in the statute — depends on total service; see our Bahrain Leaving Indemnity Calculator
The 1-day notice is the statutory floor — your contract may specify more. This applies to the private sector. Source: Bahrain LMRA — Labour Law No. 36/2012 (Art. 21) .
#### Questions
Q: How long can probation last in Bahrain?
A: Up to 3 months, extendable to 6 months only by a Ministerial decision for specified occupations. You can only be placed on probation once with the same employer.
Q: How much notice is needed to end employment during Bahrain probation?
A: At least 1 day, from either the employer or the employee, without needing to state a reason — per Article 21 of Labour Law No. 36/2012. Many contracts specify a longer notice period than this legal minimum.
Q: Do I get gratuity if terminated during probation in Bahrain?
A: The law does not contain an explicit probation-specific gratuity exclusion — gratuity (Article 116) is generally tied to your total length of service. In practice, very short probation periods rarely accrue a meaningful amount; check our Bahrain Leaving Indemnity Calculator for the general formula.
Q: Can I be placed on probation more than once by the same employer?
A: No — Bahrain law allows only one probationary period per employer for the same worker.

## Oman

### Oman Gratuity Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/oman/gratuity-calculator/
End-of-service gratuity under Oman's 2023 Labour Law (Royal Decree 53/2023) — one month of basic salary per year, with older service on the previous formula.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Service from Aug 2023 | 1 month basic salary per year
Older service (first 3 yrs) | 15 days per year
Older service (after 3 yrs) | 1 month per year
Minimum service | 1 year
Basis | Basic salary
Service on or after 1 Aug 2023 earns 1 month/year. Earlier service uses the previous 15-day/1-month formula. Source: Oman Labour Law (RD 53/2023) .
#### Questions
Q: How is gratuity calculated in Oman in 2026?
A: Under the 2023 Labour Law, one month of basic salary for each year of service from August 2023. Service before then uses the old formula: 15 days per year for the first three years and one month per year after.
Q: What is the minimum service for Oman gratuity?
A: One year of continuous service.
Q: Is Oman gratuity on basic or gross salary?
A: Basic salary only.
Q: Did Oman gratuity change in 2023?
A: Yes — Royal Decree 53/2023 raised the rate to one month per year for service from August 2023, more generous than the previous formula.

### Oman Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/oman/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused Oman annual leave — end-of-service encashment uses your comprehensive (gross) wage, under Royal Decree 53/2023.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 30 days/year
Carry-over cap | Up to 30 days may be retained/carried
Encashment during employment | Employer-optional, and paid at basic wage only, if the employee agrees in writing
Encashment on end of service | Mandatory — paid at the comprehensive (gross) wage for the unused balance
End-of-service leave encashment uses the comprehensive/gross wage — a more generous basis than the basic-wage rate that applies to optional in-service encashment. Cross-checked against Addleshaw Goddard . Source: PwC Middle East .
#### Questions
Q: How much annual leave do Oman employees earn?
A: 30 days per year under Royal Decree 53/2023, in force since 31 July 2023.
Q: What salary is used for Oman leave encashment?
A: It depends on when: optional encashment during employment (if your employer agrees) is paid at basic wage only. Mandatory encashment when your service ends uses your comprehensive (gross) wage.
Q: Can I cash out leave while still working in Oman?
A: Only if your employer agrees and you consent in writing — and only at basic wage, unlike the gross-wage rate used at end of service.
Q: Is there a cap on carrying leave forward?
A: Yes — you may retain a balance of up to 30 days; the law also requires taking at least 30 days of leave at least once every 2 years.

### Oman Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/oman/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in Oman under the new Labour Law — up from 50 days to 98 days under Royal Decree 53/2023, Article 84.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Total paid maternity leave | 98 days at full/gross wage
Split | Up to 14 days pre-delivery, remainder post-delivery
Number of occurrences | No cap (the old law's 3-time limit was removed)
Minimum prior service | None (the old law's qualifying-service requirement was removed)
Who pays | Employer pays wages; also funded via a 1% Social Protection Fund maternity-insurance contribution
This is the NEW law (effective 2023) — up from 50 days and a 3-occurrence cap under the old, repealed Royal Decree 35/2003. Source: Oman Labour Law — Royal Decree 53/2023 (Art. 84); Oman Social Protection Fund .
#### Questions
Q: How many days of paid maternity leave do I get in Oman?
A: 98 days at full wage, under Article 84 of the new Labour Law (Royal Decree 53/2023) — up from 50 days under the old, repealed law.
Q: Is there a limit on how many times I can take maternity leave in Oman?
A: No — the new law removed the old 3-occurrence cap. You can take the 98-day paid leave every time you have a child.
Q: Do I need a minimum length of service to qualify for Oman maternity leave?
A: No — the new law removed the qualifying-service requirement that existed under the old Royal Decree 35/2003.
Q: Who pays for maternity leave in Oman?
A: Your employer pays your wages during the leave; the system is transitioning to funding through Oman's Social Protection Fund, to which employers contribute 1% of wages per month toward a dedicated maternity-insurance branch.

### Oman Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/oman/notice-period-calculator/
Notice period for ending an unlimited Oman employment contract under Royal Decree 53/2023, Article 38.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Monthly-paid worker, unlimited contract | 30 days notice
Other pay frequency, unlimited contract | 15 days notice
Fixed-term contract | Generally cannot be ended early by notice — runs to term, or ends only for cause
If notice is not honoured | Compensation based on the comprehensive (gross) wage for the notice period
In force since 31 July 2023. Do not confuse this mid-term termination notice (Article 38) with the separate 1-month-plus non-renewal notice under Article 36(5). Cross-checked against Dentons . Source: Curtis, Mallet-Prevost, Colt & Mosle (Oman Law Blog) .
#### Questions
Q: How much notice is required in Oman?
A: For an unlimited (open-ended) contract: 30 days if you are paid monthly, 15 days if you are paid another way, under Article 38 of Royal Decree 53/2023.
Q: Can a fixed-term contract be ended early with notice?
A: Generally no — fixed-term contracts run to their end date, and can usually only be ended early for cause under Articles 40/41, or by mutual agreement.
Q: What salary is used for payment in lieu of notice?
A: Your comprehensive (gross) wage — not just your basic salary.
Q: Is this the same as the non-renewal notice?
A: No — Article 38 (30/15 days) covers ending an unlimited contract mid-term. A separate rule (Article 36(5)) requires at least 1 month's notice if an employer does not intend to renew a fixed-term contract.

### Oman Probation Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/oman/probation-period-calculator/
How much notice is legally required to end employment during probation in Oman, per the new Labour Law (Royal Decree 53/2023, Article 37).
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Maximum probation — monthly-paid worker | 3 months
Maximum probation — other pay basis | 2 months
Times allowed per employer | Once only
Notice to end employment during probation | At least 7 days, either party
If you complete probation | Counts toward your total length of service
This is the NEW Oman Labour Law (effective 26 July 2023), replacing the old Royal Decree 35/2003. Source: Oman Labour Law — Royal Decree 53/2023 (Art. 37) .
#### Questions
Q: How long can probation last in Oman?
A: Up to 3 months for workers paid monthly, or 2 months for workers paid on another basis — under Royal Decree 53/2023, Article 37. You can only be placed on probation once by the same employer.
Q: How much notice is needed to end employment during Oman probation?
A: At least 7 days, from either the employer or the employee, under Article 37 of the new Labour Law.
Q: Does probation count toward my service in Oman?
A: Yes — if you complete your probation period, it counts as part of your total length of service, which matters for your eventual gratuity.
Q: Is this the old or new Oman Labour Law?
A: This is the NEW law — Royal Decree 53/2023, effective 26 July 2023 — which replaced the previous Royal Decree 35/2003.

## India

### India Gratuity Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/india/gratuity-calculator/
Gratuity per the Payment of Gratuity Act — 15 days' salary for every completed year (15/26 formula), after 5 years of service, capped at ₹20 lakh.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Formula | (last salary × 15 × years) ÷ 26
Salary | Basic + dearness allowance
Eligibility | 5 years of continuous service
Year rounding | Over 6 months rounds up
Cap | ₹20,00,000 (20 lakh)
Enter basic + DA as the salary. Years round up if the extra months exceed 6. Tax-free up to ₹20 lakh. Source: Payment of Gratuity Act .
#### Questions
Q: How is gratuity calculated in India?
A: Last drawn salary (basic + dearness allowance) × 15 × completed years ÷ 26. You must complete five years, and a part-year over six months rounds up to a full year.
Q: What is the gratuity eligibility in India?
A: Five years of continuous service, except in cases of death or disablement where the five-year rule is waived.
Q: Is there a gratuity limit in India?
A: Yes — gratuity is capped and tax-exempt up to ₹20,00,000 (20 lakh).
Q: Which salary is used for Indian gratuity?
A: The last drawn basic salary plus dearness allowance — not the full CTC.

### India Leave Encashment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/india/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused earned leave — the standard Indian formula is (Basic + DA) ÷ 30 × unused days, capped at ₹25 lakh tax exemption.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Formula | (Basic salary + Dearness Allowance) ÷ 30 × unused earned-leave days
Entitlement (Factories Act, factory workers) | 1 day earned leave per 20 days worked, after 240 days worked in a year
Entitlement (other sectors) | Varies by state Shops & Establishments Act — check your state and company policy
Tax exemption (non-government employees) | Up to ₹25,00,000 lifetime aggregate, under Section 10(10AA)
Some employers use a divisor of 26 instead of 30 — check your company policy. The exact ENTITLEMENT rate (how many days you earn per year) varies by sector and state; this tool encashes the balance you already know you are owed, from your payslip or HR record. Cross-checked against HROne . Source: ClearTax .
#### Questions
Q: What is the formula for leave encashment in India?
A: (Basic salary + Dearness Allowance) ÷ 30 × the number of unused earned-leave days — though some companies use a divisor of 26 instead, so check your payslip or HR policy.
Q: Is leave encashment taxable in India?
A: At retirement/resignation for non-government employees, it is exempt up to ₹25,00,000 (a lifetime aggregate limit across employers) under Section 10(10AA); for government employees it is fully tax-free. Leave encashed while still employed is fully taxable.
Q: How many earned-leave days do I accrue per year in India?
A: This varies by sector and state — factory workers under the Factories Act 1948 earn roughly 1 day per 20 days worked (after 240 days worked in a year); other sectors follow their state's Shops & Establishments Act, which differs across states. Check your payslip or HR policy for your actual balance.
Q: Is this the same as gratuity?
A: No — see our India Gratuity Calculator for that separate, service-length-based benefit. Leave encashment pays out unused vacation days specifically.

### India Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/india/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in India, and what it's worth — per the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (as amended by the 2017 Amendment), Section 5.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
1st or 2nd child | 26 weeks (182 days) fully paid
3rd child or later | 12 weeks (84 days) fully paid
Pre-delivery cap | Up to 8 weeks may be taken before the expected delivery date
Eligibility | At least 80 days actually worked in the 12 months before the expected delivery date
Applies to | Establishments with 10 or more employees
Who pays | Employer (or ESI, if you're covered under that scheme)
Salary basis = basic salary + dearness allowance. A part-time work-from-home arrangement may also be mutually agreed after the leave, depending on your role (Sec. 5(5)). Source: Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended by the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 (Sec. 5) .
#### Questions
Q: How many weeks of maternity leave do I get in India?
A: 26 weeks (about 182 days) of fully paid leave for your first or second child, reducing to 12 weeks (84 days) from the third child onward — under Section 5 of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended in 2017.
Q: What is the eligibility requirement for maternity leave in India?
A: You must have actually worked at least 80 days in the 12 months immediately before your expected delivery date (Section 5(2)).
Q: Does India's maternity leave law apply to every employer?
A: It applies to factories, mines, plantations, shops and establishments with 10 or more employees. Smaller establishments fall outside the Act's coverage.
Q: Is Indian maternity leave paid by the employer or the government?
A: By the employer directly, under the Maternity Benefit Act. If you're covered under India's separate ESI (Employees' State Insurance) scheme, your cash maternity benefit is instead paid through ESI.
Q: Why does maternity leave reduce for a 3rd child in India?
A: The 2017 Amendment to the Act deliberately set a lower 12-week entitlement from the third child onward, while keeping the fuller 26 weeks for the first two.

## Philippines

### Philippines Leave Encashment Calculator (Service Incentive Leave)
URL: https://calcnate.com/philippines/leave-encashment-calculator/
Cash out your unused Service Incentive Leave — the only leave type the Labor Code mandates be convertible to cash, per Article 95.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Entitlement | 5 days Service Incentive Leave (SIL) per year, after 1 year of service
Who is covered | Rank-and-file employees — exempt if your company already grants 5+ paid VL days, or has fewer than 10 workers
Commutable to cash | Yes — the only Labor Code leave type that must be converted to cash if unused
Formula | Daily rate × unused SIL days
Vacation/sick leave beyond the 5-day SIL minimum is a company-policy benefit, not a Labor Code mandate — whether it is encashable depends on your employer's policy, not the law. Cross-checked against NDV Law . Source: Labor Law PH .
#### Questions
Q: What is Service Incentive Leave (SIL)?
A: A minimum 5 days of paid leave per year that the Labor Code (Article 95) guarantees to rank-and-file employees with at least 1 year of service.
Q: Is SIL the only leave that must be paid out in cash?
A: Yes — it is the only Labor Code-mandated leave type that must be commuted to cash if unused at year-end. Any additional vacation/sick leave your company grants is a policy benefit, and whether it is encashable depends on that policy.
Q: Who is exempt from SIL?
A: Companies with fewer than 10 employees, and companies that already grant 5 or more days of paid vacation leave, are exempt from the SIL mandate specifically.
Q: How is the cash value calculated?
A: Your daily rate multiplied by the number of unused SIL days.

### Philippines Maternity Leave Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/philippines/maternity-leave-calculator/
How much paid maternity leave you're entitled to in the Philippines and what it's worth — per the Expanded Maternity Leave Law, Republic Act No. 11210 (2019).
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Regular entitlement | 105 days paid, for every pregnancy — no cap on the number of children
Solo parent (RA 8972) | +15 extra days paid — 120 days total
Optional extension | +30 further days, unpaid
Eligibility | At least 3 monthly SSS contributions in the 12 months before the semester of childbirth
Who pays | SSS-funded (average daily salary credit); employer advances pay and tops up the “salary differential”
At least 60 days of the leave must be taken after delivery. Small businesses (≤10 workers) and micro-enterprises may be exempted from the salary-differential top-up. Source: Republic Act No. 11210, the Expanded Maternity Leave Law (2019) .
#### Questions
Q: How many days of paid maternity leave do I get in the Philippines?
A: 105 days for every pregnancy, under the Expanded Maternity Leave Law (RA 11210) — rising to 120 days if you're a qualified solo parent under RA 8972. An additional 30 days may be taken unpaid if you choose.
Q: Is there a limit on how many children this applies to in the Philippines?
A: No — unlike some countries, RA 11210 grants the full 105 days for every single pregnancy, with no reduction after a certain number of children.
Q: Who pays for maternity leave in the Philippines?
A: The Social Security System (SSS), based on your average daily salary credit. Your employer advances the payment and is reimbursed by SSS, and must separately pay you the difference between your actual salary and the SSS benefit (the ‘salary differential’), unless exempted as a small or distressed business.
Q: What's the eligibility requirement for Philippine maternity leave?
A: At least 3 monthly SSS contributions in the 12-month period immediately before the semester of your childbirth, miscarriage, or emergency termination of pregnancy.

### Philippines Notice Period Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/philippines/notice-period-calculator/
The Philippines has three distinct notice-period regimes under the Labor Code depending on why the job is ending — this tool tells you which applies.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Authorized-cause termination (redundancy, retrenchment, closure, labour-saving devices) | 30 days advance written notice to BOTH the employee and DOLE — mandatory (Art. 298)
Just-cause dismissal (misconduct, fraud, etc.) | No fixed advance-notice period — twin-notice due process instead (Art. 297)
Employee resignation | 30 days written notice, waivable at the employer's discretion (Art. 300)
Article numbers use the Labor Code's renumbered scheme (formerly Articles 283, 282 and 285). These are three separate legal regimes — do not apply one figure to all termination types. Cross-checked against Respicio & Co. . Source: Labor Law PH .
#### Questions
Q: How much notice does an employer need to give in the Philippines?
A: It depends on why: 30 days advance written notice to both the employee and DOLE for an authorized-cause termination (redundancy, retrenchment, closure, labour-saving devices, Article 298); no fixed advance notice for a just-cause dismissal, but a twin-notice due-process procedure instead (Article 297).
Q: How much notice must I give if I resign?
A: At least 30 days written notice under Article 300, though your employer can choose to waive this.
Q: Can my employer just pay me instead of giving 30 days notice for redundancy?
A: No — the 30-day advance notice to you and DOLE is a mandatory procedural step for authorized-cause termination, not something that can simply be paid away. Skipping it can expose the employer to nominal-damages liability on top of your separation pay.
Q: What is twin-notice due process?
A: For a just-cause dismissal, the employer must give a written notice of the specific charge, a real opportunity to respond, and then a written notice of the decision — rather than a fixed advance-notice period.
Q: Is separation pay the same as notice pay?
A: No — they are different. See our Philippines Separation Pay Calculator for the redundancy/retrenchment payout; this tool covers the notice/procedural requirement only.

### Philippines Probationary Employment Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/philippines/probation-period-calculator/
What notice and pay apply if your employment ends during probation in the Philippines — per the Labor Code, Article 296 (formerly Article 281).
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Maximum probation length | 6 months from your start date (unless a longer apprenticeship agreement applies)
Valid grounds to end probation early | (a) Just cause, or (b) failure to meet reasonable standards made known to you at hiring
Notice — failure to meet standards | No fixed number of days; written notice within a reasonable time, no hearing required
Notice — just cause | Standard twin-notice + hearing (same due process as regular employees)
Separation pay — standards/just cause | Not owed
Separation pay — authorized cause (redundancy, closure, etc.) | Owed — same formula as regular employees, even during probation
If you work beyond 6 months without being told you failed to qualify, you generally become a regular employee by operation of law. Source: Philippine Labor Code, Article 296 (formerly 281) .
#### Questions
Q: How long can probationary employment last in the Philippines?
A: A maximum of 6 months from your start date, under Labor Code Article 296 (formerly Article 281), unless you're covered by a longer apprenticeship agreement.
Q: Can my employer end my probation without notice in the Philippines?
A: Not quite — for failure to meet standards, written notice of which standard you failed must be given within a reasonable time before the effective date (no fixed number of days, and no hearing is required by law). For just-cause termination, the standard twin-notice-and-hearing due process applies, same as for regular employees.
Q: Do I get separation pay if I'm let go during probation in the Philippines?
A: Generally no, if it's for just cause or for failing to meet standards. You DO get separation pay if the reason is an authorized cause — redundancy, retrenchment, closure, or disease — using the same formula as a regular employee, even though you're still on probation.
Q: What happens if my probation isn't formally ended after 6 months?
A: If you continue working past 6 months without your employer telling you that you failed to qualify as a regular employee, you generally become a regular employee by operation of law.

### Philippines Separation Pay Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/philippines/separation-pay-calculator/
Separation pay and retirement pay under the Philippine Labor Code — the amount depends on the cause of separation.
#### How it is calculated
Service | Entitlement
Redundancy / labour-saving | 1 month pay per year
Retrenchment / closure / disease | ½ month pay per year
Minimum separation pay | 1 month
Retirement (60–65, 5+ yrs) | 22.5 days pay per year
Voluntary resignation | Generally none
Separation pay applies to authorized-cause dismissals, not voluntary resignation. A part-year of 6 months or more counts as a full year. Source: Philippine Labor Code .
#### Questions
Q: How is separation pay calculated in the Philippines?
A: For authorized-cause dismissals: one month's pay per year of service for redundancy or labour-saving devices, or half a month per year for retrenchment, closure or disease — with a one-month minimum. A part-year of six months or more counts as one year.
Q: Do I get separation pay if I resign?
A: Generally no. Voluntary resignation does not entitle you to separation pay unless your contract or CBA provides it.
Q: How is retirement pay calculated?
A: For employees aged 60–65 with at least five years of service, retirement pay is 22.5 days of pay per year of service (half-month salary equivalent).
Q: What counts as a full year for separation pay?
A: A fraction of at least six months is counted as one whole year.

## United Kingdom

### UK Holiday Pay on Leaving Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uk/holiday-pay-calculator/
Work out the accrued-but-untaken holiday your employer must pay you when you leave — the pro-rata (A×B)−C rule from the Working Time Regulations 1998.
#### How it is calculated
Rule | Detail
Statutory entitlement | 5.6 weeks per year (28 days for a 5-day week)
On leaving | Accrued minus taken, paid in lieu
Accrual formula | entitlement × (proportion of leave year worked) − taken
A day's pay | A week's pay ÷ working days per week
Pay basis | Normal remuneration (regular overtime/commission included)
Regulation 14 pays accrued untaken statutory leave when the job ends. A 'week's pay' for variable pay uses a 52-week average (ERA 1996 ss.221–224). Source: Working Time Regulations 1998, reg 14 .
#### Questions
Q: Do I get paid for unused holiday when I leave a job in the UK?
A: Yes. Under the Working Time Regulations 1998 (regulation 14), any statutory holiday you've accrued but not taken by your last day must be paid in lieu. The amount is your accrued entitlement for the part-year worked, minus holiday already taken, valued at a day's pay.
Q: How is accrued holiday calculated on leaving?
A: Take your annual entitlement (statutory minimum 5.6 weeks, i.e. 28 days for a five-day week), multiply by the proportion of the holiday year you worked before leaving, then subtract the days you already took. What's left is paid out.
Q: Can my employer make me take holiday during my notice?
A: Yes — an employer can require you to use accrued holiday during your notice period by giving the correct notice (twice the length of the leave). Holiday taken this way reduces what's paid out.
Q: What if I've taken more holiday than I accrued?
A: If you've taken more statutory leave than you'd accrued by your leaving date, your employer can only recover the excess if your contract or a written agreement clearly allows a deduction. Without that, they generally cannot claw it back.
Q: Is holiday pay based on basic pay only?
A: No. Holiday pay must reflect your 'normal remuneration', which includes regular overtime, commission and similar payments. For variable pay, a week's pay is averaged over the previous 52 worked weeks.

### UK Statutory Notice Pay Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uk/notice-pay-calculator/
The statutory minimum notice your employer must give — and what it's worth in pay. Per the Employment Rights Act 1996, section 86.
#### How it is calculated
Rule | Detail
1 month up to under 2 years | 1 week (employer)
2 years up to under 12 years | 1 week per complete year (employer)
12 years or more | 12 weeks (employer cap)
Employee resigning | 1 week after 1 month (does not rise with service)
Pay basis | Normal full pay — no weekly cap
This is the statutory minimum. A contract can require longer notice, in which case the contractual period applies. Source: GOV.UK — Notice periods .
#### Questions
Q: How much notice must my employer give me in the UK?
A: The statutory minimum is one week if you've worked between one month and two years, then one week for every complete year, capped at 12 weeks (so 12 years' service or more gives 12 weeks). Your contract may require more, in which case the longer period applies.
Q: How much notice must I give when I resign?
A: The statutory minimum for an employee is one week once you've been employed for at least one month, and it does not increase with length of service. Your contract will often require more — commonly one month for many roles.
Q: Is notice pay capped like redundancy pay?
A: No. Notice pay is your normal full weekly pay for each week of notice. The statutory weekly-pay cap (£751 in 2026/27) applies to redundancy pay, not to notice pay.
Q: What is payment in lieu of notice (PILON)?
A: Instead of working your notice, your employer can pay you the wages you would have earned during the notice period. PILON is generally taxable as earnings.
Q: Do I get statutory notice if I'm dismissed for gross misconduct?
A: No. An employer can dismiss without notice (summary dismissal) for genuine gross misconduct. Statutory notice applies to ordinary dismissals, including redundancy.

### UK Notice Period Calculator — Work Out Your Last Day
URL: https://calcnate.com/uk/notice-period-calculator/
Enter the date you hand in (or receive) notice and the notice length — 1 week, 4 weeks, 1 month, or the statutory minimum — and get your exact last day of employment, with working days and bank holidays counted.
#### How a UK notice period is counted
Rule | Detail
Day 1 of notice | The day after notice is given (ACAS). Hand in notice on Monday → notice runs from Tuesday.
Notice in weeks | Ends on the same weekday N weeks after the day notice was given. 1 week's notice given Monday → last day the following Monday.
Notice in months | Ends on the corresponding date in a later month. 1 month's notice given 5 June → last day 5 July. No matching date (e.g. 31 Jan) → last day of the following month.
Weekends & bank holidays | Count towards the notice period — it's calendar time, not working days.
Last day on a non-working day | Employment still ends that date; your final day physically at work is the working day before.
Sources: ACAS — Notice periods · GOV.UK — Handing in your notice · GOV.UK — Redundancy notice periods .
#### Questions
Q: When does my notice period actually start?
A: Per ACAS guidance, a notice period normally starts the day AFTER you give notice, not the day itself. So if you hand in your notice on Monday, day one of your notice period is Tuesday — and one week's notice would make the following Monday your last day.
Q: Does a notice period include weekends and bank holidays?
A: Yes. A notice period is measured in calendar time, so weekends and bank holidays count towards it. They only matter for which days you actually work: your last day of employment can fall on a non-working day, in which case your final working day is the last working day before it.
Q: Is 4 weeks' notice the same as 1 month's notice?
A: No. Four weeks is always exactly 28 days, while one month runs to the same date in the next month (the "corresponding date" rule) — which is 28 to 31 days depending on the month. Over a 3-month notice period the difference between "12 weeks" and "3 months" can be several days, so check the exact wording in your contract.
Q: How is 1 month's notice counted if there is no matching date next month?
A: One month's notice ends on the corresponding date in the next month — notice given 5 June ends 5 July. If there is no corresponding date (for example one month from 31 January), the period ends on the last day of the following month (28 or 29 February).
Q: What if my last day of notice falls on a weekend?
A: Your employment still legally ends on that date — the notice period is calendar time. In practice your final day in work is simply the last working day before it, and you remain employed (and paid) through to the end date.
Q: How much notice do I have to give by law in the UK?
A: The statutory minimum for an employee resigning is 1 week once you have at least one month's service — it does not increase with length of service. Most contracts require more (commonly one month). An employer dismissing you must give 1 week after one month's service, rising to 1 week per complete year from 2 years, capped at 12 weeks.
Q: Can my employer make me leave before my notice period ends?
A: Only if your contract allows payment in lieu of notice (PILON) — paying you what you would have earned for the remaining notice instead of you working it — or puts you on garden leave, where you stay employed and paid to the end date but do not attend work. Otherwise, ending your employment early without pay for the notice owed can be wrongful dismissal.
Q: What happens if I leave without working my full notice?
A: You would be in breach of contract. In practice most employers do not sue, but they can refuse to pay for time not worked, may deduct losses where the contract allows, and it can cost you a good reference. It is almost always better to agree an earlier leaving date in writing.

### UK Statutory Redundancy Pay Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/uk/redundancy-pay-calculator/
How much statutory redundancy pay you are owed — age-banded weeks capped at 20 years and the statutory weekly-pay limit. England, Wales & Scotland (Employment Rights Act 1996).
#### How it is calculated
Rule | Detail
Aged 41 and over | 1.5 weeks' pay per full year
Aged 22 to 40 | 1 week's pay per full year
Under 22 | 0.5 week's pay per full year
Years counted | Most recent 20 years only
Weekly pay cap | £751 (from 6 Apr 2026); £719 (2025/26)
Maximum payment | £22,530 (2026/27); £21,570 (2025/26)
Minimum service | 2 years' continuous employment
Each year is banded by the age you were during that year, working back from your current age. Weekly pay is gross, averaged over the 12 weeks before notice, and capped at the statutory limit. Source: GOV.UK — Redundancy pay .
#### Questions
Q: How is UK statutory redundancy pay calculated?
A: For each full year of continuous service you get 1.5 weeks' pay for years you were 41 or over, 1 week's pay for years you were 22 to 40, and half a week's pay for years under 22. Only your most recent 20 years count, and weekly pay is capped at the statutory limit (£751 from 6 April 2026, £719 for 2025/26).
Q: What is the maximum statutory redundancy payment?
A: The maximum is 30 weeks' pay at the capped weekly rate: £22,530 for redundancies on or after 6 April 2026 (20 years × 1.5 weeks × £751), and £21,570 for 2025/26 (× £719).
Q: Do I qualify for statutory redundancy pay?
A: You must have at least two years of continuous service with the employer and be an employee (not self-employed or a genuine contractor). Some dismissals — such as being offered suitable alternative work you unreasonably refuse — can remove the entitlement.
Q: Is redundancy pay based on gross or net pay?
A: Gross pay — your average weekly earnings before tax over the 12 weeks before you were given notice, capped at the statutory weekly limit. Statutory redundancy pay itself is tax-free up to £30,000.
Q: Does my employer have to give more than statutory?
A: Statutory is the legal minimum. Many employers pay enhanced (contractual) redundancy that is more generous — check your contract or company policy. This calculator shows the statutory floor.

## Canada

### Canada Termination & Severance Pay Calculator
URL: https://calcnate.com/canada/severance-pay-calculator/
The statutory MINIMUM you're owed when let go — notice/termination pay plus severance pay — under the Ontario ESA or the federal Canada Labour Code. Common-law reasonable notice is often higher.
#### How it is calculated
Rule | Detail
Ontario notice | <1yr=1wk, 1–3yr=2, then 1 wk/yr, cap 8 weeks (after 3 months)
Ontario severance | 1 week/year (+ months÷12), cap 26 — only if 5+ yrs AND payroll ≥ $2.5M (or 50+ let go)
Federal notice | 2 weeks from 3 months; 3 weeks at 3 yrs; +1 wk/yr, cap 8 (since 1 Feb 2024)
Federal severance | Greater of 2 days' wages/year or 5 days' wages — after 12 months
Basis | Regular wages for a regular work week
These are STATUTORY MINIMUMS. In Ontario, termination pay and severance pay are separate and can both apply. Common-law 'reasonable notice' is often significantly more. Source: ontario.ca / canada.ca .
#### Questions
Q: How is severance pay calculated in Ontario?
A: Ontario ESA severance pay is one week of regular wages for each completed year of employment, plus a fraction for extra months (months ÷ 12), capped at 26 weeks. It applies only if you worked 5+ years AND the employer's payroll is at least $2.5 million (or 50+ employees were severed within six months). It is separate from, and paid on top of, termination (notice) pay.
Q: What's the difference between termination pay and severance pay in Ontario?
A: Termination pay replaces the notice period (1 week per year up to 8 weeks). Severance pay is an extra entitlement for long-service employees of larger employers (1 week per year up to 26 weeks). A qualifying employee can receive both.
Q: What is federal severance under the Canada Labour Code?
A: For federally regulated employees (banks, airlines, telecoms, interprovincial transport, etc.), after 12 months you're owed the greater of two days' wages per year of service or five days' wages, on top of graduated notice of 2–8 weeks.
Q: Is the statutory amount all I can get?
